name: Postgres store facade
purpose: The single project-side module that imports the pg driver, exposes narrow named domain verbs to consumer code, issues every query as a static string literal with $N parameters, and emits structured lifecycle events to the injected event sink. Consumers never destructure the pg driver outside this module; the facade is the one place the vendor surface lives. The driver reference is opaque at this boundary so the round-6 Hyperdrive v1.1.0 adapter (ADR-2801) can swap the client without a facade re-shape.
responsibilities: Open a pg.Pool on boot against the elicited connection URL; hold no other reference to the pg vendor surface; export no symbol that leaks the raw pool or client (AC-27101-1, AC-27101-2).

Expose named domain verbs (getUserById, createUser, listUsers, ...) as named exports with typed parameters; refuse a general-purpose raw-SQL passthrough on the public surface (AC-27101-1, AC-27103-1).

Issue every read and write through pg.query with a static string literal as the first argument and parameters as an array bound to $1, $2, ... $N per the node-postgres parameterised-queries contract (AC-27103-1).

Expose the transaction helper (TAC-2803) as a named verb; consumers pass a callback, the helper wraps BEGIN and COMMIT, ROLLBACK on error, and fires transactionRolledBack on the sink with the failing statement index (AC-27104-1).
Emit facadeReady exactly once per facade instance on the injected event sink with the database name; serialise pre-ready consumer queries behind the pool's ready-check (AC-27101-1, AC-27108-1).
Expose the optional advisory-lock helper only when the elicited answer is session or transaction; the surface is absent when the answer is off (AC-27107-1).
internalStructure: One module exporting a createStore({ connectionUrl, onEvent, poolConfig, advisoryLockHelper }) factory returning a Store whose methods are the named CRUD verbs plus withTransaction and (optionally) withAdvisoryLock. The pg import lives at the top of this module; the factory captures a pg.Pool and the injected sink and hands back closures. Consumers destructure the verbs they need at their top level and hold the facade reference for the process lifetime (or, on a request-scoped container platform, for the request lifetime).

interfaces.name: createStore
interfaces.description: createStore({ connectionUrl, onEvent, poolConfig, advisoryLockHelper }) -> Store. The sole entry point every consumer calls. Opens a pg.Pool against connectionUrl; wires the sink; hands back a Store whose methods are the named CRUD verbs plus withTransaction and (optionally) withAdvisoryLock.

interfaces.name: onEvent
interfaces.description: Structured-event sink invoked with { event, ts, ... } for facadeReady, migrationsApplied, transactionRolledBack, backupExported, recoveryDrillPassed, queryFailed events. Never invoked with domain-row values.

interfaces.name: store.verbs
interfaces.description: The named domain CRUD verbs the facade exposes. Each verb has typed parameters; no verb accepts a raw SQL string or a general query object from consumer code.

dependencies.name: Migration runner
dependencies.description: The runner the facade or the CI step invokes to apply forward-only migrations before the facade opens its first query.

dependencies.name: Transaction helper
dependencies.description: The helper wrapping BEGIN and COMMIT around a consumer callback; exposed as store.withTransaction.

dependencies.name: Recovery runner
dependencies.description: Shares the facade's event sink for backupExported and recoveryDrillPassed events; invoked from the ops or CI surface, not from request code.

tradeoffs: The facade holds a long-lived pool on Node targets and a request-scoped pool on container targets; the round-6 Hyperdrive adapter (ADR-2801) delegates the pool entirely to the Hyperdrive-managed pool. That flexibility costs a per-target pool decision the operator makes via ADR-2805; the facade's outward interface stays unchanged across all three postures.
